headline: Border Negotiator Confirms ‘Structural Differences’ Are Just A Misplaced IKEA Instruction Manual
body:
A senior diplomatic negotiator revealed today that the much-discussed 'structural differences' hindering high-level bilateral talks are not geopolitical in nature, but simply a missing bag of screws from a flat-pack bookshelf assembly started by both nations in 1962.

“We’ve been sitting across the table for decades, and it turns out we’re just holding two different translated versions of a diagram for a Kallax unit,” said Ramesh Gupta, a mid-level attaché who spent the morning scouring the border floor for a spare wooden dowel. “The Chinese side is convinced we have the L-shaped bracket, and we’re fairly certain they walked off with the Allen key three administrations ago.”

Independent observers noted that the tension at the negotiation table vanished momentarily when both delegations realized they were trying to assemble the same unit upside down. While a resolution to the shelf is pending, both teams have agreed to pause further border posturing until a local hardware store can provide a universal fastener that satisfies the sovereignty of both cabinets.
caption: It turns out the biggest geopolitical crisis of our time was just an unfinished DIY project. Maybe we should check the spare parts bin under the table? 🛠️🌏 #Diplomacy #IKEAProblems #Geopolitics #BorderTalks (satire)
igHook: Have you ever let a missing screw ruin your entire weekend, too?

On the table, scattered amidst several thick binders and microphones, lies a single small, L-shaped metal Allen key and a confusing black-and-white furniture assembly instruction sheet.
